source.document_id: ISO 26262-5:2018 Road vehicles - Functional safety - Part 5: Product development at the hardware level; 8.4.5 Table 4 (SPFM targets), 8.4.6 Table 5 (LFM targets), 9.4.2.2 Table 6 (PMHF targets), Annex C equations C.1..C.8, Annex B fault classification

note: H-09 (issue #56) target-value extract for docs/hw/fmeda.md and tools/fmeda-calculator.py (OR-004). The licensed standard is not retained in the repository (source_pdf_hash null; source_url is the ISO catalogue page). The target values below are the widely published Table 4/5/6 values, corroborated by public secondary sources cited in the tool-qualification record (TI SLYP685 slide 'Hardware metrics'; Chalmers 2023 thesis sections 4.4.2-4.4.4). Citation disposition (issue #56 wording): Annex D of ISO 26262-5:2018 supplies the diagnostic-coverage classes (low 60 % / medium 90 % / high 99 %, Table D.1 and the per-element Tables D.2..D.14); the standard's worked SPFM/LFM example is Annex E (Table E.1) and the PMHF example is Annex F. Table E.1 row data has NOT been transcribed from a licensed copy and is therefore not part of the regression; this is the declared TCL2 validation gap of the fmeda tool. Project note: issue #56 sets a stricter PMHF target of 1e-8 /h for the ASIL-B alignment; Table 6 assigns 1e-8 /h to ASIL D and 1e-7 /h to ASIL B and C - both are reported.
